name: LocalizationCsv
src_typeComment: Converts between a translator's spreadsheet and the toolkit's key -> text tables.  THE SHEET SHAPE IS ONE COLUMN PER LANGUAGE, one row per key:  key,en,fr,de ui.start,Start,Démarrer,Starten ui.quit,Quit,Quitter,  which is the shape a translator is actually handed, because every language sits side by side and an untranslated cell is visibly blank. Note this is TRANSPOSED relative to CsvToScriptableObjectImporter, whose columns are FIELDS of one asset per row — that tool cannot read this shape, which is why the localisation importer is its own window. The CSV parsing itself is the existing CsvUtility, so quoted commas and newlines inside a translated sentence are handled here for free.  A blank cell means NOT TRANSLATED, not "empty string" — it is skipped entirely so the fallback locale fills the gap. A translator's half-finished sheet is the normal case, not an error.

src_members.comment: The round trip: hand a translator back a sheet containing every key that currently exists, with the translations already done filled in and the rest blank. This is how new keys reach them without anyone diffing asset files by hand.

src_members.name: ToCsv
src_members.comment: alignColumns pads each column to a common width so the file reads as a TABLE in a plain text editor instead of a wall of commas — which is the difference between a file you can proofread and one you can only load into a spreadsheet. The padding is plain spaces placed AFTER each comma, so the result is still valid CSV and ParseRows trims it straight back off.  The trade-off, stated plainly: open an aligned file in Excel and the padding shows up as leading spaces inside the cells. Export unaligned when the file is going straight to a translator working in a spreadsheet; export aligned when a person is going to READ it.
